title: Africa FX Update
dek: The naira’s official-versus-parallel spread remains the key West African FX watch as the rand softens and Egypt’s pound stays under pressure.
spotlightText: Nigeria parallel-market premium — roughly ₦38/$ above the official reference.
body: Nigeria’s parallel market remains the day’s standout divergence. AMB calculates a consensus benchmark only when at least two reasonably current independent observations are available, and discloses material source dispersion instead of smoothing it away.

The rand is trading softer on the day, while Egypt’s pound remains closely watched after another modest move lower. Ghana and Kenya continue to provide relatively stable official benchmarks for West and East Africa.
take: The naira spread is still contained versus earlier periods, but the persistence of a parallel premium keeps liquidity and price-discovery risk in focus.

title: Naira Holds, Rand Firms
dek: Nigeria’s official FX rate stayed broadly stable while South Africa’s rand found support as global risk appetite improved.
spotlightText: Nigeria official-to-parallel spread narrowed modestly into the weekend.
body: Nigeria ended the prior session with a relatively orderly official market, while the parallel market remained higher but without the kind of dislocation seen in earlier periods.
The rand gained modestly against the dollar as global market tone improved, helping offset some of the week’s earlier weakness.
take: A narrowing Nigeria spread is constructive, but durability matters more than a single-session move.

title: October Opens With Mixed FX Signals
dek: African currencies opened October with a split picture: the naira stayed range-bound, the cedi remained steady, and the rand moved with global risk sentiment.
spotlightText: Parallel premium remained elevated but stable.
body: The first session of October brought no major break in Nigeria’s FX pattern, with official and parallel markets both remaining within recent ranges.
Ghana and Kenya were steady, while South Africa continued to show the strongest sensitivity to broader dollar and risk-on/risk-off moves.
take: October begins without a major FX shock, but external dollar strength remains the swing factor for the region’s more liquid currencies.

title: Month-End FX Check
dek: September closed with African FX markets calmer than mid-quarter, but liquidity and inflation risks remain uneven across the continent.
spotlightText: Nigeria ended September with a manageable but persistent parallel premium.
body: Month-end trading showed a broadly calmer tone across the region, with fewer abrupt dislocations than seen earlier in the quarter.
Still, policy credibility, dollar liquidity and inflation differentials remain the key drivers heading into October.
take: Stability improved into month-end, but the next test is whether that carries into a fresh quarter.
